newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares close slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: French shares close slightly lower.

text.p: French shares closed slightly lower due to a lower domestic bond market and despite gains on Wall Street, dealers said.
Bond prices fell due to resurgent doubts over whether France can hit its deficit reduction targets.

Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said in a statement late in the afternoon the government was set on strictly respecting the targest of reducing the deficit to three percent of GDP in 1997 and 2.8 percent in 1998.
The CAC-40 index closed 5.79 points, or 0.22 percent, lower at 2,615.18.
The market was also affected by political worries with rumours of a dissolution of Parliament, traders said.

"As the factors that usually determine the trend in France were on green -- the dollar, the German bunds, the Treasury-bond and Wall Street. The only explication for the slide are the rumours about a dissolution of parliament," a broker at a British brokerage in Paris.
Despite official denials a government reshuffle or parliament dissolution -- for early elections -- was on the cards, rumours were rife about a Chirac move.
* Volume was 6.6 billion francs, of which 5.14 billion was in CAC-40 shares.
The market opened higher but ran quickly out of steam when it neared resistance at 2,650 and turned lower after a day's high of 2,644.81 points.
Favourable U.S. data -- jobless claims, international trade and the Philadelphia Fed index -- briefly breathed some spirit in the market but the index soon returned to negative territory.
